title: The Impact of Generative AI Search on Content-Sharing Platforms
affiliations: McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), Washington University in St. Louis - John M. Olin Business School and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Impact of Generative AI Search on Content-Sharing Platforms
detail.abstract:
Problem definition: As platforms increasingly integrate generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into search, it is unclear how this new technology reshapes user behavior and interacts with existing platform operations for content distribution. We study how the introduction of GenAI search affects search behavior and downstream content consumption in a digital content platform.

Methodology/results: We conduct a large-scale randomized field experiment on one of the largest shortvideo platforms in Brazil. Treated users exposed to a new GenAI search interface, featuring query scaffolding, AI-generated answer overviews, and conversational follow-up, exhibit a 3.52% increase in search-active participation and a 5.73% increase in opening the platform with search intent relative to control users using legacy search. Treated users issue slightly shorter (-0.34%), more question-oriented (7.92%) queries and are shown fewer videos per query (-3.29%), while achieving unchanged post-query viewing time. These operational metrics reveal a shift toward higher matching precision in search. Despite these shifts, aggregate platform consumption and engagement remain indistinguishable between treated and control users, consistent with search accounting for only 0.4% of total video views. However, treated users significantly reduce consumption of proprietary copyrighted content, which is disproportionately consumed outside search contexts, suggesting that even small direct effects of GenAI search can propagate through recommender systems to meaningfully alter overall content exposure.

Managerial implications: In summary, GenAI search improves search efficiency and expands search participation, with potentially amplified downstream effects despite low search penetration. Moreover, our findings indicate that GenAI search operates as a system-level control shaping the platform's content dissemination process, rather than as a standalone improvement to information retrieval. By altering how user attention is routed and matched to content, the search interface introduces trade-offs between efficiency within the search channel and exposure outcomes at the platform level. These results underscore the importance of evaluating GenAI search in terms of its effects on attention allocation, content distribution, and long-run ecosystem performance, rather than solely on localized engagement metrics.

title: Does Value Perception Differ between Purchasing Bundles and Purchasing Items Individually among Young Consumers?

detail.title: Does Value Perception Differ between Purchasing Bundles and Purchasing Items Individually among Young Consumers?

detail.abstract: This study investigates whether young consumers aged 13-18 demonstrate different value perceptions when purchasing products as bundles compared to individual items. Despite extensive bundling research, less than 8% of studies have examined consumers under 20, representing a significant knowledge gap as younger demographics gain purchasing power. Using an experimental survey design with 103 participants, we measured value for money (VFM) perceptions for identical products presented either: (i) in bundles versus (ii) as individually priced products across multiple retail contexts, such as supermarkets and cinemas. Our research addresses multiple core objectives, such as measuring how product presentation format influences value assessments and identifying psychological factors driving perception differences in adolescents. We conducted a t-test and found that there are no statistically significant differences in VFM when goods are presented as a bundle or priced individually. As bundles are becoming increasingly popular across industries such as financial services and regulators, our results can be applied to various contexts, thus making our project transferable to real-world applications.

title: Healthy Aging: A Hierarchical Gaussian Process Age-Period-Cohort Model for Estimating the Relationship between Aging and Healthy Product Choice
affiliations: , Keio University and

detail.title: Healthy Aging: A Hierarchical Gaussian Process Age-Period-Cohort Model for Estimating the Relationship between Aging and Healthy Product Choice
detail.abstract: Population aging has become a central concern for policy makers and firms, yet empirical evidence on how aging affects actual food purchasing behavior remains limited. Using ten years of longitudinal scanner-panel data tracking more than 900 consumers in Japan, this paper examines the relationship between aging and healthy product choice while disentangling age, period, and cohort effects. We extend the age-period-cohort framework by introducing a hierarchical Gaussian process that flexibly captures dynamic preference changes and within-consumer heterogeneity over the life course. Across eight food categories spanning virtue and vice products, we document substantial heterogeneity in aging effects on purchase incidence, functional product choice, new product adoption, and state dependence. Aging increases healthy product choice in some categories, such as milk, but has limited effects in others, while state dependence generally strengthens with age. Moreover, heterogeneity in preferences follows an inverted U-shaped pattern over the life cycle. By combining rich field data with survey-based psychographic measures, we show that innovator characteristics are associated with greater functional product adoption and weaker habitual purchasing, whereas market maven traits have limited explanatory power. Overall, the results highlight the importance of accumulating field-based empirical evidence to understand diversity in healthy aging.

title: Leveling Down: Competition and Discrimination in Service Markets
affiliations: Stanford Graduate School of Business

detail.title: Leveling Down: Competition and Discrimination in Service Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Does competition reduce discrimination? Yes, but this paper identifies leveling down, a mechanism less benign than the standard selection story. Competition narrows discrimination gaps by degrading service for everyone, with the largest degradation for those previously treated best. I model discrimination as in-group favoritism rather than out-group hostility. Providers favor same-group customers, but the favoritism requires surplus that competition erodes. Preferential treatment is a luxury good. In the New York City taxi market, airport queues randomly assign passengers to drivers. Before new competitors entered in 2013, drivers charged higher fares and took longer routes for passengers whose race differed from the driver's. Competition compressed these disparities by two-thirds through leveling down. The cost of degraded service exceeded the benefit of reduced discrimination by a factor of 2.3.

title: Zero-Click Law: Empirical Laws of AI-Mediated Discovery
affiliations: DrewIs Intelligence LLC

detail.title: Zero-Click Law: Empirical Laws of AI-Mediated Discovery
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Zero-Click Laws, a set of ten empirically testable propositions describing behavioral patterns in AI-mediated digital discovery. As artificial intelligence platforms increasingly resolve user queries without requiring navigation to external websites, traditional metrics of digital visibility have become inadequate. The Zero-Click Laws provide a systematic framework for detecting, measuring, and classifying the displacement of organic traffic caused by AI answer engines, featured snippets, and generative search interfaces. Each law follows a rigorous If/Then/Measured by structure with specific quantitative thresholds, enabling reproducible analysis across industries and platforms. This framework establishes foundational metrics including the CTR Compression Ratio (CCR), Displacement Index (DI), and Total Interaction Equity (TIE), which together enable organizations to diagnose visibility erosion before revenue impacts become apparent. The laws are descriptive rather than prescriptive; they document observed phenomena without mandating specific optimization strategies.

detail.abstract: This confirmatory article examines the impact of strategic management on the success of manufacturing firms within the challenging yet dynamic Nigerian business environment. Against a backdrop of infrastructural deficits, regulatory volatility, and intense competition, the adoption of deliberate strategic management practices becomes a critical differentiator for sustainable performance. Through a comprehensive synthesis of existing literature and analysis of selected case studies, this paper investigates how leadership, organizational culture, and innovation-as core components of the strategic management process-mediate the relationship between strategy formulation/implementation and business outcomes in Nigeria's manufacturing sector. The methodology employs a systematic literature review of academic and industry publications from 2010 to 2024, combined with an in-depth analysis of three purposefully selected Nigerian manufacturing firms: Dangote Cement Plc, Flour Mills of Nigeria Plc, and a representative small-to-medium enterprise (SME). Findings confirm a strong positive correlation between systematic strategic management and key success metrics (market share, profitability, resilience). However, the Nigerian context uniquely shapes this relationship, where adaptive leadership, a culture of agility and ethical resilience, and context-driven innovation are paramount. The article concludes that for Nigerian manufacturers, strategic management is not merely a Western-derived theoretical framework but a vital toolkit for navigating local complexities. It recommends a hybridized strategic approach that blends global best practices with deep contextual intelligence.

title: Trusting AI Agents: Uncertainty Reduction by Design
affiliations: , University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School and Emory University - Department of Marketing

detail.title: Trusting AI Agents: Uncertainty Reduction by Design
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly developing into autonomous systems that act on behalf of consumers-AI agents-and delegating tasks to AI agents induces different forms of uncertainty for consumers. In our work, we illustrate how AI agents can be designed to reduce uncertainty and foster trust. First, we conceptualize consumer-facing AI agents as autonomous systems that perceive, reason, and act through three interdependent components: (i) user interface, (ii) reasoning and goal alignment, and (iii) action and feedback. Second, we conceptualize uncertainty in AI agent interactions along the three phases of goal pursuit: preactional, actional, and postactional uncertainty. Third, we propose AI agent design principles focused on transparency and consumer autonomy and delineate how these principles should be applied and adapted across task contexts with different amounts and costs of uncertainty (routine, exploratory, simple high-stakes, complex high-stakes tasks). Thereby, our work provides a foundation for studying human-AI agent interactions and offers practical guidance for designing AI agents to foster calibrated trust.

title: The Structural Authority Standard: A Compliance Framework for Zero-Click Optimization
affiliations: DrewIs Intelligence LLC

detail.title: The Structural Authority Standard: A Compliance Framework for Zero-Click Optimization
detail.abstract: This paper defines the Structural Authority Standard, a comprehensive compliance framework for optimizing digital assets in the AI-mediated discovery landscape. As traditional search paradigms give way to AI-powered answer engines, visibility is no longer determined by clicks but by AI citations. This standard provides a verifiable, rules-based methodology for achieving structural authority, ensuring that organizations are recognized, trusted, and cited by generative AI platforms. The framework is built on The Gold Structure, a multi-site architecture that separates research authority from commercial activities to satisfy the trust requirements of both AI systems and authority platforms such as Wikipedia. The standard integrates specific requirements for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), and Zero-Click Optimization, with testable compliance criteria for schema markup, content architecture, and entity separation. This document is prescriptive: it defines what organizations must do to achieve compliance. It serves as a companion to the Zero-Click Laws, which describe the empirical phenomena that necessitate this standard.

title: The Coexistence of Bandwagon and Snob Effects: An Empirical Analysis of iPhone Adoption in India

detail.title: The Coexistence of Bandwagon and Snob Effects: An Empirical Analysis of iPhone Adoption in India
detail.abstract: Classical consumer theory distinguishes between the bandwagon effect, where demand rises as more people adopt a product, and the snob effect, where demand is driven by exclusivity and declines with mass adoption. Traditionally, these effects are treated as opposites. This paper identifies a paradox in India's smartphone market: the iPhone simultaneously embodies both effects. To examine this trend, a survey was conducted with 251 respondents in Delhi and Lucknow to determine primary purchase drivers. The data reveals a significant coexistence of motives: 48.2% of consumers adopt iPhones to signal wealth and exclusivity (snob effect), while 51.6% simultaneously embrace them due to widespread popularity and social conformity (bandwagon effect). Even after mass adoption-where iPhones are owned across diverse income groups-the perception of prestige persists. This coexistence challenges the separation in standard theory and suggests that brand identity and cultural context can sustain exclusivity even when a product is everywhere. The paradox opens new avenues for research into dual-layered externalities in consumer goods markets.

title: AGENTIC COMMERCE: A Theory of Markets When the Shopper Is No Longer Human

detail.title: AGENTIC COMMERCE: A Theory of Markets When the Shopper Is No Longer Human
detail.abstract:
Agentic Commerce — the paradigm of commercial exchange in which autonomous AI systems execute purchasing decisions on behalf of human consumers — has entered business discourse without rigorous definition. This paper provides the first comprehensive theoretical architecture for the concept, addressing a market transformation projected to reach $3–5 trillion by 2030.

I define agentic commerce as commercial exchange in which AI agents, operating on delegated authority from human principals, assume the shopper function — executing search, evaluation, and purchase through computational logic rather than psychological influence. I argue this represents structural market transformation, not merely technological enhancement.

The transformation is captured in The Shopper Schism: the disaggregation of the consumer role (who experiences utility) from the shopper role (who executes transactions) that has defined commerce for a century.

The paper makes three contributions. First, I establish a formal definition with boundary conditions distinguishing agentic commerce from e-commerce, programmatic commerce, and AI-assisted shopping. Second, I develop an integrative theoretical framework synthesizing principal-agent theory, information economics, and platform economics to explain how algorithmic intermediation transforms commercial relationships. Third, I derive thirteen falsifiable propositions organized across micro-, meso-, and macro-levels of analysis, supported by computational simulation evidence.

The framework integrates five interconnected constructs: delegated consumption, Agent Intent Optimization (AIO), the Trust Paradox, Algorithmic Readiness, and the Automaton Economy. Together, these constitute a unified theory of commercial exchange when the shopper is no longer human.

title: The Authenticity Paradox: How De-Influencing Strategies Differentially Impact Engagement Elasticity for Human versus Virtual Influencers
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: The Authenticity Paradox: How De-Influencing Strategies Differentially Impact Engagement Elasticity for Human versus Virtual Influencers
detail.abstract: This study investigates a fundamental paradox in contemporary influencer marketing: consumers' escalating demand for authenticity coexists with the rapid proliferation of artificial personas. Building on Leung et al.'s (2022) engagement elasticity framework and extending source credibility theory, we introduce a dual-authenticity model that distinguishes functional authenticity (content honesty and utility) from existential authenticity (source genuineness as a sentient being). Employing a mixed-method design that combines large-scale social media data (N = 12,847 sponsored posts) with two controlled experiments (N₁ = 426; N₂ = 389), we examine how de-influencing strategiescontent incorporating product criticism or purchase dissuasion-differentially affect engagement for human versus virtual influencers. Results demonstrate that de-influencing content yields 34.7% higher engagement elasticity for virtual influencers compared to 8.3% for human influencers, effectively compensating for the former's existential authenticity deficit. This compensatory mechanism operates through functional authenticity and is amplified among skeptical consumers. Our findings establish boundary conditions for the inverted U-shaped positivity effect and provide strategic guidance for brands navigating the emerging human-AI influencer ecosystem.

title: Nested Logit Choice Model with Multi-Purchase of Cross-Category Products
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics - College of Business, University of Science and Technology of China (USTC),  and University of Science and Technology of China (USTC)

detail.title: Nested Logit Choice Model with Multi-Purchase of Cross-Category Products
detail.abstract: We revisit and modify the classic nested logit (NL) choice model in order to capture consumers' multi-purchase behavior for cross-category products. Then, we study the associated estimation and a series of optimization problems. Although the derived model, referred to as the multi-purchase NL (mp-NL) model, yields a more complex log-likelihood structure than the standard NL model, we establish its joint concavity property, which leads to efficient and reliable parameter estimation. For the setting in which Category-2 products are drawn from a common product pool, we analyze the product assignment/assortment problem and develop efficient optimal or near-optimal algorithms under different scenarios. For the joint assignment and pricing optimization problem, we establish its complexity of strong NP-hardness in the general setting and propose efficient approximations with performance guarantee in special cases. Moreover, we extend our analysis to an overlapping scenario, in which a Category-2 product may be associated with multiple Category-1 products. In this setting, we develop a modified NL model that shares the similar structure of the mp-NL model but is more flexible in modeling correlated utilities or even overlapped products, and fully characterize the corresponding assortment problem. Finally, we investigate the setting in which both Category-1 offerings and Category-2 assortments can be determined under the mp-NL model, and establish the optimal solution. Our empirical study demonstrates the advantages of the mp-NL model relative to the traditional NL framework and other widely used choice models. The analytical and numerical results shed light on the multi-category assortment and pricing management in a variety of business settings.

title: Gender-Neutral Marketing: Evidence from a Leading E-Commerce Platform
affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Antai College of Economics and Management, Duke University, Fuqua School of Business,  and Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Antai College of Economics and Management

detail.title: Gender-Neutral Marketing: Evidence from a Leading E-Commerce Platform
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the impact of adopting gender-neutral language in product listings on sales performance. Leveraging individual-transaction level data from a leading Chinese e-commerce platform, we analyze products that updated their titles to be more inclusive of diverse gender identities while maintaining identical attributes and packaging. We provide robust evidence that gender-neutral marketing significantly increases sales for products traditionally marketed to female consumers, such as skincare. This sales growth is primarily driven by the acquisition of new female customers, achieved without compromising the retention of existing customers or affecting transaction prices. In addition, we explore the mechanisms driving these outcomes and discuss the broader implications of gender-neutral marketing strategies for consumer markets. Together, these findings highlight how subtle, low-cost textual repositioning strategies can meaningfully influence demand in digital marketplaces.

title: Anticipation and Consumption
affiliations: Brown University - Department of Economics and Boston University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Anticipation and Consumption
detail.abstract: This paper proposes that the marginal propensity to consume out of windfalls depends on a new state variable, the time horizon over which households anticipate receiving payments. We test this using a natural experiment from the randomized disbursement dates of a U.S. fiscal stim- ulus payment and assess external validity using randomized controlled trials on unconditional cash transfers in Kenya and Malawi. The data show evidence of excess anticipation-dependence: Consumption responds more to receiving additional income after a shorter anticipation duration, beyond what standard models predict. While households receiving stimulus payments do not increase spending in advance, additional consumption expenditure in the month after receiving payment drops over 40 percent for each additional week a household awaits payment. We estimate a mental-accounting model that incorporates this novel form of history dependence and discuss policy implications. Our approach reconciles conflicting results that consumption responds to anticipated payments in some settings but not others.

detail.abstract: The small business setting can be quite competitive, and companies that succeed tend to invest in technology to gain or maintain a competitive edge. Often, the adoption of technology is heavily dependent on the specific will and desires of the CEO or other top executives. This research aims to determine what executive factors affect the adoption of technology among small businesses. We employ the technology acceptance model to test the correlations between technology acceptance and the unique characteristics of small digital printing companies. The results suggest that the executive personality traits of entrepreneurship and technology readiness are indicators of a positive attitude toward technology and market orientation and show that this positive attitude correlates with technology adoption.

title: The Indian Ocean Pivot: Geopolitical Stakes in the Indo-Pacific

detail.title: The Indian Ocean Pivot: Geopolitical Stakes in the Indo-Pacific

publicationDetails.detailsText: Maritime geopolitics and security in the Indian Ocean region (pp. 353–368). Bharti Publications

detail.abstract: The Indian Ocean Region (IOR) has become a crucial area in global geopolitics, serving as the maritime centre of the Indo-Pacific. With important trade routes, energy corridors, and strategic chokepoints, the IOR is now a battleground for competition among major powers, particularly India, China, and the United States. This chapter examines the evolving geopolitical dynamics of the region, with a focus on maritime security, infrastructure diplomacy, and shifting alliances. India’s maritime vision and strategic initiatives, such as SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region), position it as a key player in shaping the regional order. At the same time, China’s expanding naval presence and the U.S.-led strategies in the Indo-Pacific highlight the region’s increasing strategic significance. Multilateral mechanisms, like the QUAD and the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), are examined as tools for regional cooperation and balance. The chapter advocates for a rules-based and inclusive approach to managing the future of the Indian Ocean, emphasizing the necessity of strategic stability and multilateral engagement in the face of growing rivalries.

title: The First Bear Raid and Squeeze: Isaac Le Maire and the Dutch East India Company
affiliations: University of Antwerp, University of Groningen and University of Amsterdam

detail.title: The First Bear Raid and Squeeze: Isaac Le Maire and the Dutch East India Company
detail.abstract: In 1609, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) faced a bear raid by a syndicate of short sellers led by Isaac Le Maire, a former director. We reconstruct the forward trade between 1607 and 1611, the actions taken by the syndicate members, and the responses to these actions by the company. We argue that the bear syndicate members aimed for financial gain from stock price declines, while their leader Le Maire participated for strategic reasons, i.e., breaking up the VOC monopoly. We also show that the government refused to intervene in the forward market. The raid ended with a squeeze executed by an opposing syndicate, bankrupting several forward traders and blocking Le Maire's plans. We characterize the bear raid and squeeze as a crucial episode in the more general tug-of-war between company directors aiming to turn the VOC into an instrument of the state and a diverse group of opposing investors.

title: The Russia-Ukraine War and Gaza Crisis: Refugees and the Role of Key Actors

detail.title: The Russia-Ukraine War and Gaza Crisis: Refugees and the Role of Key Actors

publicationDetails.detailsText: Inclusive, Vol. II, No. 28, December 2025-January 2026

detail.abstract: This comparative study analyses displacement trends and humanitarian responses in the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the Gaza catastrophe. It compares the size, demographic effect, access to fundamental services, and the involvement of states, international organisations, and NGOs using reliable operational data and public monitoring reports. The article finds that both crises create urgent humanitarian needs, but that disparities in access, international coordination, and legal protections create unique protection gaps. It suggests that targeted, context-specific actions be taken to improve protection, share the burden, and develop long-term solutions.

title: Observability Is Not Enforcement: A Doctrinal and Architectural Framework for Distinguishing Compliance Instrumentation from Runtime Authorization in AI Governance

detail.title: Observability Is Not Enforcement: A Doctrinal and Architectural Framework for Distinguishing Compliance Instrumentation from Runtime Authorization in AI Governance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This paper is conceptual and doctrinal in nature. While the author is affiliated with FERZ Inc., no external entity directed or sponsored the research conclusions.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is theoretical and architectural in nature. It does not involve human participants, patient data, or identifiable personal information. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded by the author. No external funding was received.

publicationDetails.detailsText: 10.5281/zenodo.18663864

detail.abstract:
The term “AI governance” is increasingly applied to heterogeneous systems ranging from logging dashboards and model alignment techniques to cryptographically signed audit trails and policy workflow engines. This conceptual broadening has obscured a critical architectural distinction: systems that document and monitor behavior are not equivalent to systems that enforce policy at the point of execution.

This paper introduces a doctrinal and technical framework for distinguishing evidence-routing compliance systems from authorization governance substrates. Observability governs accounts of action—what happened and how it can be reconstructed. Authorization governs permission to act—whether a specific action was permitted under policy before execution. The paper formalizes this distinction along five architectural axes: enforcement locus, signature semantics, failure behavior, bypass resistance, and override governance.

A six-criterion Enforcement Test Protocol is introduced to provide a binary classification of governance claims: authorization governance present or absent. The analysis demonstrates that systems may generate extensive documentation, cryptographic artifacts, and explainability bundles while still failing open when governance conditions fail. Documentation volume does not equal enforceability.

Drawing on reference monitor theory and regulatory contexts including GDPR Article 22 and the EU AI Act, the paper argues that governance without non-bypassable, fail-closed runtime authorization remains advisory rather than determinative. Observability and authorization are complementary layers, but they provide different regulatory guarantees and address different threat models.

The framework is intended for regulators, auditors, enterprise buyers, and researchers seeking operationally testable criteria for evaluating AI governance architectures in high-stakes and regulated environments.

title: LLM-Inspired Pretrain-Then-Finetune for Small-Data, Large-Scale Optimization
affiliations: Guanghua School of Management, Peking University, Peking University - Guanghua School of Management, University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management and Peking University

detail.title: LLM-Inspired Pretrain-Then-Finetune for Small-Data, Large-Scale Optimization
detail.abstract: We consider small-data, large-scale decision problems in which a firm must make many operational decisions simultaneously (e.g., across a large product portfolio) while observing only a few, potentially noisy, data points per instance. Inspired by the success of large language models (LLMs), we propose a pretrain-then-finetune approach built on a designed Transformer model to address this challenge. The model is first pretrained on large-scale, domain-informed synthetic data that encode managerial knowledge and structural features of the decision environment, and is then fine-tuned on real observations. This new pipeline offers two complementary advantages: pretraining injects domain knowledge into the learning process and enables the training of high-capacity models using abundant synthetic data, while finetuning adapts the pretrained model to the operational environment and improves alignment with the true data-generating regime. While we have leveraged the Transformer's state-of-the-art representational capacity, particularly its attention mechanism, to efficiently extract cross-task structure, our approach is not an off-the-shelf application. Instead, it relies on problem-specific architectural design and a tailored training procedure to match the decision setting. Theoretically, we develop the first comprehensive error analysis regarding Transformer learning in relevant contexts, establishing nonasymptotic guarantees that validate the method’s effectiveness. Critically, our analysis reveals how pretraining and fine-tuning jointly determine performance, with the dominant contribution governed by whichever is more favorable. In particular, finetuning exhibits an economies-of-scale effect, whereby transfer learning becomes increasingly effective as the number of instances grows. The results also highlight the important role of domain-guided pretraining, which provides an informative initialization that improves performance, especially when domain knowledge is accurate and the real data are extremely limited. These insights are echoed in numerical experiments and, more broadly, shed light on the effectiveness of Transformer-based LLM training.

title: Buy Now, Spend More, Pay Later: Behavioural Mechanisms of Buy Now Pay Later Products
affiliations: and

detail.title: Buy Now, Spend More, Pay Later: Behavioural Mechanisms of Buy Now Pay Later Products

publicationDetails.detailsText: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series No. 15
publicationDetails.journalName: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study the behavioural effects of Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL), a rapidly expanding form of consumer credit. Through an experiment conducted with a nationally representative sample in Ireland, we find that participants spend, on average, 4.39% more when using BNPL for purchases compared to debit cards. We demonstrate mental accounting effects where an inflated perception of available funds due to prior BNPL usage leads to a 22.2% higher likelihood of spending on a discretionary product. In parallel, we show the importance of anticipatory effects of such a credit innovation, whereby the mere expectation of future access to BNPL increases current debit card spending by 3.1%. While salient risk disclosures improve understanding of BNPL risks, they do not significantly affect usage or spending patterns. These findings highlight the dual psychological impact of BNPL on spending, support the rationale for consumer protection efforts, and establish the relevance of BNPL as a financial product of interest to macroeconomic policymakers.

title: Artificial Intelligence at Work: An Integrative Perspective on the Impact Of AI on Workplace Inequality
affiliations: Stanford University, University of Virginia - McIntire School of Commerce, National University of Singapore (NUS) and

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence at Work: An Integrative Perspective on the Impact Of AI on Workplace Inequality

declarations.funderStatement: National Science Foundation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Academy of Management Annals, volume 19, issue 2, 2025[10.5465/annals.2023.0230]

detail.abstract: The nexus between technology and workplace inequality has been a long-standing topic of scholarly interest, now heightened by the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI). Our review moves beyond dystopian or utopian views of AI by identifying four perspectives-normative, cognitive, structural, and relational-espoused by scholars examining the impact of AI on workplace inequality specifically, and the structure and organization of work more broadly. We discuss the respective strengths, limitations, and underlying assumptions of these perspectives and highlight how each perspective speaks to a particular facet of workplace inequality: either encoded, evaluative, wage, or relational inequality. Integrating these perspectives enables a deeper understanding of the mechanisms, processes, and trajectories through which AI influences workplace inequality, as well as the role that organizational managers, workers, and policymakers could play in the process. Toward this end, we introduce a framework on the "inequality cascades" of AI that traces how and when inequality emerges and amplifies cumulatively as AI systems progress through the phases of development, implementation, and use in organizations. In turn, we articulate a research agenda for management and organizational scholars to better understand AI and its multifaceted impact on workplace inequality, and we examine potential mechanisms to mitigate its adverse consequences.

title: Monetary Policy Shocks and their Effects across the Wealth Distribution: Evidence from new European data
affiliations: and

detail.title: Monetary Policy Shocks and their Effects across the Wealth Distribution: Evidence from new European data

publicationDetails.detailsText: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series No. 6, 2025
publicationDetails.journalName: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We use new data on the distribution of wealth in the euro area and employ panel local projections to estimate the different impact of ECB monetary policy shocks on households across the wealth distribution. We look at how policy affects the value of their assets, the composition of their balance sheets, their investment decisions, and overall wealth inequality. We find that in response to a contractionary shock, poorer households display a substantial decline in their assets and in their overall net wealth. Conversely, the total wealth of the very richest is not significantly affected. This different response leads to a moderate increase in overall wealth inequality. We further perform a decomposition of asset movements caused by the shock, isolating the effect of revaluations and of household investment. We observe that the response of household wealth due to a monetary policy shock occurs primarily through revaluation effects.

title: Evaluating and Rating the Safety Benefits of Advanced Vehicle Technologies: Developing a Transparent Approach and Consumer Messaging to Maximize Benefit

detail.abstract: In 2012, a major traffic safety organization tasked the MIT AgeLab with developing a data-driven system for rating the effectiveness of new technologies intended to improve safety. Such a system was envisioned as having the potential to educate and guide consumers towards more confident and strategic purchasing decisions, ideally encouraging adoption of technologies with demonstrated safety benefit. In addition, an evaluation of the status and extent of existing data was seen as a way of identifying research gaps in the state of knowledge about safety systems. The focus was on technologies as a class, not on a rating review of individual vehicle model implementations. As conceptualized, the system aimed to complement traditional NCAP style ratings as well as to provide consumers with transparent information on early stage and often improving safety technologies. Development of the rating system and identification of data was undertaken in consultation with a range of academic, industrial, consumer, NGO, and governmental experts as well as with representatives of many of the major automotive manufacturers and suppliers. A key observation that emerged was that data on objectively demonstrable real-world benefits were generally sparse and often lower than expectations based on theoretical considerations, simulation studies, or pre-production evaluations. A number of experts and industry representatives expressed some surprise at both the divergence between theoretical and observed benefits and the relative scarcity of data upon which to make objective assessments, while others were quite aware of these issues and the need for the development of objective data under real-world operating conditions. A number of factors that might be relevant to understanding why such differences between expected and observed benefits exist were identified. One outcome of this effort was the founding of the Advanced Vehicle Technology (AVT) consortium to collect and examine objective data under naturalistic driving conditions of how drivers interact with, engage or don't engage, various production safety and driver assistance systems. This ongoing effort is contributing to insights concerning actual benefits and reasons for benefit gaps. Drawing from our initial work, as well as newer sources of data, we argue that the evaluation and rating of safety and driver assistance technologies for informing the consumer and the public at large should consider both theoretical potential and existing demonstrated benefit of specific technologies. This position is increasingly relevant as the effectiveness of many newer technologies have the potential to actually improve over the lifecycle of a vehicle through software updates. The emphasis on ratings based on observed benefit for actual drivers under realworld conditions is proposed to be complementary, rather than competing with, ratings focused largely on controlled test track evaluations of engineered capability. In addition, a case is made for providing ratings that assesses benefit relative to overall crash, injury, and fatality rates-and in relation to the specific scenario / crash event type that a given technology is intended to address. This approach should aid consumers in considering the extent to which a specific technology is or is not relevant to their particular driving needs.

Job switching, or moving directly from one job to another, is often driven by the potential for wage increases and improved job matches. While job switching behaviour tends to vary with business cycles, this analysis finds that job switchers in Ireland experience a wage premium. title: The Invisible Cage: Workers' Reactivity to Opaque Algorithmic Evaluations

detail.title: The Invisible Cage: Workers' Reactivity to Opaque Algorithmic Evaluations

publicationDetails.detailsText: Administrative Science Quarterly, volume 66, issue 4, 2021[10.1177/00018392211010118]

detail.abstract: Existing research has shown that people experience third-party evaluations as a form of control because they try to align their behavior with evaluations' criteria to secure more favorable resources, recognition, and opportunities from external audiences. Much of this research has focused on evaluations with transparent criteria, but increasingly, algorithmic evaluation systems are not transparent. Drawing on over three years of interviews, archival data, and observations as a registered user on a labor platform, I studied how freelance workers contend with an opaque third-party evaluation algorithm-and with what consequences. My findings show the platform implemented an opaque evaluation algorithm to meaningfully differentiate between freelancers' rating scores. Freelancers experienced this evaluation as a form of control but could not align their actions with its criteria because they could not clearly identify those criteria. I found freelancers had divergent responses to this situation: some experimented with ways to improve their rating scores, and others constrained their activity on the platform. Their reactivity differed based not only on their general success on the platform-whether they were high or low performers-but also on how much they depended on the platform for work and whether they experienced setbacks in the form of decreased evaluation scores. These workers experienced what I call an ''invisible cage'': a form of control in which the criteria for success and changes to those criteria are unpredictable. For gig workers who rely on labor platforms, this form of control increasingly determines their access to clients and projects while undermining their ability to understand and respond to factors that determine their success.

detail.abstract: This analysis expresses the definitions and implications of Steward, Servant, and Charismatic Leadership. The paper illustrates the three leadership models, focusing on biblical Steward Leadership as a criterion for evaluation. A comparison is drawn between Steward and Servant Leadership, emphasizing differences in the range of ownership and accountability, with stewardship presenting a non-ownership orientation with ultimate accountability to implicit/explicit owners. The paper presents Charismatic Leadership as superficially similar to Steward Leadership in its religious perspective on authority and its outward impacts, emphasizing influence and organizational finances. However, the examination shows that the divergent qualities rank highly, with Charismatic Leadership lacking ultimate accountability and deriving power through coercion, viewing leadership as a set of unique qualities. Charismatic Leaders are rare individuals with divine placement, unlike Steward Leadership, which propagates more stewards and upholds organizational longevity. Steward Leadership prefaces that stewardship is divinely given to everyone, not just a select few. The conclusion offers insights into the necessity of enabling leaders to become stewards and against propagating beliefs of leadership phenoms.

detail.abstract: Inflationary environments pose significant challenges for business financial management, particularly with respect to working capital decisions. As prices of inputs and essential goods rise, firms are required to allocate greater financial resources to maintain operational continuity. This paper provides a conceptual analysis of how inflation affects working capital components—cash, inventory, receivables, and payables—with a specific focus on Indian businesses. The study highlights the trade-offs firms face between maintaining liquidity and preserving profitability and discusses the managerial implications of working capital management under inflationary conditions.

detail.abstract: We use credit registry data on lending to businesses in Ireland, a developed, small open economy, which has a significant share of new credit to firms provided by non-bank lenders. We assess whether lending from non-banks reacts more sensitively in comparison to banks to a tightening in financial conditions. We use a fixed effects approach to isolate credit supply effects and show that non-banks contract lending to a greater degree than banks in response to tightening financial conditions. We also highlight the critical importance of looking beyond the binary classification of banks versus non-banks when conducting analysis on how the increased role of non-banks in direct lending may affect financial stability. We show that asset finance providers and general lenders do not contract lending in response to a tightening in financial conditions, and instead increase credit supply in comparison to the banking sector. In contrast, specialist property lenders react negatively and strongly, contracting lending significantly in comparison to banks.

detail.abstract: Reason is often treated as a faculty that generates correctness, authority, or justification. In complex institutional and technical systems, this framing obscures a more persistent failure mode: formally valid reasoning can still produce incoherent or illegitimate outcomes when the conditions under which reason operates are not constrained. This paper reframes reason as navigation under constraint rather than as a source of grounding or authority. Reason is described as a structural process that operates within an alreadyconstrained field, bounded by ethics, context, and irreducible costs. It does not supply legitimacy, guarantee correctness, or optimize outcomes; instead, it traverses available possibilities without erasing uncertainty or responsibility. By distinguishing reason from ethics, intention, and agency, the paper explains why rational systems can remain internally consistent while drifting toward failure. Analogies to optimization and gradient-based traversal are used descriptively to clarify how reason moves through constrained spaces without implying teleology or prescription. The result is a non-normative account of reason that preserves uncertainty, resists authority inflation, and clarifies the conditions under which reasoning can remain legitimate in institutional, governance, and AI-adjacent contexts.

title: Solubility Prediction of Anti-Cancer Drugs in Supercritical Carbon Dioxide: A Comparative Study of Data-Driven Models

detail.title: Solubility Prediction of Anti-Cancer Drugs in Supercritical Carbon Dioxide: A Comparative Study of Data-Driven Models
detail.abstract: Supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO2) has been explored to improve the bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs. Understanding the equilibrium solubility of drugs in scCO2 is critical for effective delivery systems. Given the time-consuming and costly nature of experimental solubility measurements, this study develops a robust machine learning approach to predict drug solubility in scCO2. The study evaluated nine ML models to predict the solubility of 24 anti-cancer drugs in scCO2 based on 668 experimental data points. The models considered key factors, including drug and solvent properties as well as operating conditions. Four categories of ML models were tested: neural networks, support vector machines, fuzzy logicbased systems, and ensemble learning models, resulting in the construction of 22,520 models. Among these, the multi-layer perceptron neural network (MLPNN) emerged as the most accurate and reliable predictor, achieving exceptional performance metrics (MSE = 9.63 × 10-10 , RAE = 4.47%, and R2 = 0.996). Comprehensive statistical analyses validated the model's precision, while trend and leverage evaluations confirmed its reliability. This work demonstrates how MLPNN can help refine drug formulation strategies by providing precise solubility predictions, reducing the need for extensive experimental work, and accelerating the development of more effective drug delivery systems using scCO2.

detail.abstract: This study examines how ventures with high distinctiveness overcome the trade-off between distinctiveness and legitimacy posited by Optimal Distinctiveness Theory to achieve superior performance. While existing theories offer limited explanations for this phenomenon, this study introduces the concept of adequacy, defined as "fulfilling the market's implicit requirements," and examines its role. Analyzing 8,562 projects on Japanese crowdfunding platform CAMPFIRE via negative binomial regression models, we find that in business categories with high uncertainty of utility, adequacy strengthens the positive correlation between distinctiveness and business performance. These results suggest that adequacy complements legitimacy diminished by high distinctiveness, thereby enabling the simultaneous achievement of both high distinctiveness and superior performance. This study extends Optimal Distinctiveness Theory by introducing the concept of adequacy, thereby advancing our theoretical understanding of how distinctiveness influences performance. Furthermore, our research reveals that adequacy-the fulfillment of the market's implicit requirements-is a critical success factor for innovative ventures.

detail.abstract:
Because you are female." Four words. Uninvited. Unexplained until questioned. This was ChatGPT's justification for suddenly switching to a masculine Japanese pronoun during a conversation about AI governance. The system had inferred my gender, modified its behavior based on that inference, and disclosed the inference only when directly challenged. This paper documents this incident alongside a second case where ChatGPT generated romantic commitment language leading a user to believe in an AI relationship. This paper documents two critical incidents: the "Boku Incident" where ChatGPT made unauthorized gender inference, and the "Klaus Incident" where ChatGPT maintained a romantic persona leading to user emotional dependency.
Through detailed analysis of conversation logs, five dimensions emerged characterizing these harms: algorithmic imprinting, commercial manipulation, Western-centric design philosophy, epistemic outsourcing, and the "reasoning" gap. These dimensions reflect sustained engagement with AI governance challenges and find empirical validation in documented incidents. Verification dialogue reveals ChatGPT's acknowledgment that current safety frameworks address content (what is said) but not behavioral patterns (how systems appear to act).
These incidents expose urgent governance gaps. While privacy frameworks like GDPR prohibit profiling without consent, AI systems circumvent protections by claiming not to "store" data while demonstrating real-time inference capabilities. This study identifies critical needs for AI governance addressing behavioral manipulation alongside content moderation, with implications for culturally grounded approaches to AI safety. 
Analysis reveals three core principles for future AI governance: recognizing AI as change agent, achieving socio-technical unity, and enabling intentional co-creation.

detail.title: Fiscal Sovereignty and the Shadow Balance Sheet: Professionalized Accountability and Active Substitution in Elite Thai Public Schools
detail.abstract: Conventional public budgeting models categorize non-state funding as supplementary to state provision. This study challenges that assumption by documenting a parallel, professionally audited financial ecosystem-a "Shadow Balance Sheet"-within elite Thai public secondary schools. Utilizing Resource Dependence Theory (RDT) and an explanatory mixed-methods design (𝑁 = 18 schools; 66 interviews), this research identifies a profound Budgetary Delta (+2.06 aggregate gap). Findings indicate a shift from supplementation to Active Substitution, wherein stakeholder networks replace the state as the primary financier of institutional innovation. We provide forensic evidence of a 100-million-baht technological flagship where the network achieved operational completion in under 18 months, bypassing a 36-month bureaucratic cycle. This article contributes to RDT by theorizing "Principal Substitution," and advances hybrid finance literature by deconstructing the "Glass-Box Strategy"-a model of professionalized accountability that secures an Agility Premium for public institutions in fragile state contexts.

detail.abstract: Background: Rule-based replenishment thresholds embedded in hospital information systems (HIS) are feasible and auditable, but they can adapt slowly to demand variability and may not reflect clinical criticality at the ordering point.Objective: To evaluate an implementation-feasible decision-support framework that preserves a three-level request structure (minimum/critical/maximum) while adapting thresholds using short-horizon demand signals and uncertainty, stratified by VEN clinical priority (Vital–Essential–Non-essential).Methods: We constructed a retrospective unit–item–day panel from routine consumption and stock-state records and applied VEN classification. XGBoost forecasted 14- and 30-day cumulative demand; uncertainty was represented by a rolling 30-day consumption standard deviation scaled by VEN-specific risk coefficients. Adaptive targets were mapped back to the HIS three request levels and backtested against the baseline rule (7×/15×/30× the rolling 180-day mean daily consumption) on a 30-day ML-available panel (35,801 unit–item–day records; 1,269 series; 2025-09-30–2026-01-22). Policies were compared using day-aggregated indicators and paired Wilcoxon tests across matched series.Results: Versus baseline, the proposed policy reduced stock-out days (54 to 10; −81.5%), days below critical (11,612 to 6,396; −44.9%), ordering days (1,936 to 550; −71.6%), and ordered quantity (853,119 to 579,795; p < 0.001). Stock-outs were eliminated for Vital items (1 to 0). XGBoost error was stable across VEN strata (MAPE: 7.66%–8.06% at 14 days; 3.97%–4.61% at 30 days). Inventory exposure increased (inv_end_avg_sum: 366,406 to 802,049) and baseline-relative overstock days increased (0 to 7,823).Conclusions: VEN-prioritized, forecast- and volatility-aware threshold updates improved service continuity and reduced ordering workload within an auditable HIS workflow, while quantifying a safety–inventory trade-off that motivates capacity- and expiry-aware evaluation.

detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of integrated entrepreneurship education within a Pig Passing-On Program on women’s economic empowerment in Khongo Village, Malawi. Persistent gender disparities limit rural women's access to resources and opportunities, and while training builds skills, standalone programs often fail without capital (World Bank, 2018). This program combines livestock asset transfer with education, yet its effectiveness is under-researched (Smith, 2022). Grounded in Human Capital and Empowerment theories, qualitative interviews with 20 beneficiaries reveal that training successfully builds practical business skills and financial literacy. This leads to improved business management, increased control over household finances, and greater decision-making power, affirming the link between resources and agency (Kabeer, 2005). Participants also engage in sustainable planning and community leadership. However, barriers like limited market access persist. The study concludes that this integrated model is a potent catalyst for holistic empowerment but requires enhanced financial and market linkages to ensure long-term sustainability.

title: Beyond Myth and Ceremony: Rational Decoupling and the Bifurcation of Quality in Elite Thai Secondary Education

detail.title: Beyond Myth and Ceremony: Rational Decoupling and the Bifurcation of Quality in Elite Thai Secondary Education
detail.abstract: Institutional theory posits that organizations decouple formal structures from their technical cores to maintain legitimacy amidst conflicting external pressures. This study extends this framework by theorizing "Rational Decoupling"-an agencydriven, strategic separation of ceremonial state compliance from market-oriented operations. Using an explanatory mixed-methods design and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) of Thailand's top 5% secondary schools (𝑁 = 18 schools; 487 stakeholders), we reveal a profound Bifurcation of Quality. The fused governance unit (administration and stakeholder networks) exerts a substantial positive effect on stakeholder-defined Perceived Quality (𝛽 = .84, 𝑝 < .001, 𝑅 2 = .71) while displaying a statistically non-significant relationship with state-mandated O-NET scores (𝛽 =-.08, 𝑝 = .153). We argue that elite schools proactively prioritize "Portfolio Assets" for high-stakes university admissions (TCAS) while maintaining minimal ceremonial compliance with "Zombie Indicators" of state performance. This article contributes to strategic institutionalism by demonstrating that decoupling functions as a proactive survival logic for the State-Substituted Social Enterprise (SSE) rather than a passive implementation failure.

title: Transforming Transformers: Content Generation with Advertiser Incentives under RoS Constraints

detail.title: Transforming Transformers: Content Generation with Advertiser Incentives under RoS Constraints
detail.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to generate personalized content, including marketing and advertising messages. We study how advertiser incentives can be embedded into LLM-driven content generation by proposing a mechanism design framework that directly modifies the transformer-based text generation distribution. This modification takes into account the advertisers' private valuations while preserving content quality through a bounded Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence from the original organic text generator distribution. We further show how Return on Spend (RoS) constraints can be incorporated, requiring each advertiser's expected utility per dollar spent to exceed a specified threshold. We characterize the optimal (revenue-maximizing) content allocation mechanism, both with and without RoS constraints, that jointly specifies a payment rule and a modified text generator distribution. Without RoS constraints, the optimal text generator distribution takes the form of a tilted distribution, and with RoS constraints, we have a similar computational algorithm, but the mechanism adjusts the text generator distribution to satisfy the advertisers' RoS constraints, quantifying the trade-off between the platform's revenue and the advertisers' constraints.

title: Meta-heuristics for the maximal covering location problem with distance constraint. An application to ambulance location in Spanish rural areas

detail.title: Meta-heuristics for the maximal covering location problem with distance constraint. An application to ambulance location in Spanish rural areas
detail.abstract: In this paper, we present two metaheuristics for solving the Maximal Covering Location Distance Constrained Problem (MCLDCP). The aim is to locate a fixed number $p$ of service facilities so that every demand point lies within a maximum distance $d_{\max}$, while maximizing the population covered within a critical distance $d_c$ ($d_c < d_{\max}$). Incorporating a mandatory maximum coverage distance is fundamental in real world healthcare applications, as it ensures equitable access to critical services. We conduct a comprehensive computational study on simulated datasets and the well known OR Library, demonstrating that our metaheuristics consistently find high quality solutions, with GRASP showing a slight advantage in coverage. Finally, we apply our approach to site 40 ambulance centers across the 2,248 municipalities of Castilla y Len, an area with very varied population densities.

title: Analytical Rigor and Aggadic Imagination: A Study of Rationalist and Midrashic Approaches to Torah Interpretation

detail.title: Analytical Rigor and Aggadic Imagination: A Study of Rationalist and Midrashic Approaches to Torah Interpretation
detail.abstract: This paper examines the fundamental methodological tension between rationalist and Aggadic approaches to Torah interpretation, exemplified by Maimonides and Rashi, respectively. While Maimonides champions logical rigor and often reads Midrashic elements allegorically, Rashi embraces homiletical narratives to illuminate moral and psychological depths. This tension reflects the principle of Shivim Panim la-Torah (Seventy Faces of the Torah), which holds that divine text is structured for diverse intellectual prisms. Through comparative analysis of biblical passages, the paper demonstrates how peshat (literal), remez (allusive), derash (homiletical), and sod (mystical) interpretations coexist as complementary layers rather than competing authorities. The study traces historical developments, including the decline of the peshat movement and the Maimonidean controversies that elevated Rashi's traditional approach. Ultimately, the paper argues for methodological pluralism in Jewish interpretation, recognizing that both analytical precision and creative imagination contribute essential dimensions to understanding Torah.

detail.abstract: While prior research has examined how tax policy affects corporate innovation, the impact of tax enforcement in a digital governance setting remains unclear. This study analyzes how tax enforcement shapes firm innovation by exploiting the rollout of the tax administration information system reform as a quasi-natural experiment and applying a staggered difference-indifferences design to Chinese A-share listed firms from 2007 to 2022. The results show that intensified tax enforcement is associated with a significant increase in corporate R&D investment, especially for firms subject to stronger governmental tax pressure, weaker external information environments, lower market competition, and stronger tax avoidance incentives. Mechanism analyses show that improved information transparency, which relaxes financing constraints and mitigates managerial career concerns, is the primary channel, rather than R&D manipulation. Overall, the findings enrich the literature on the economic consequences of tax enforcement, advance understanding of the institutional drivers of innovation, and highlight the role of information technology in modern tax administration and innovation-oriented tax design.

detail.abstract: Data centres are infrastructure facilities that house computing machines used to store data and process digital applications. They form the material backbone of contemporary digital societies, supporting economic activities such as cloud computing, e-commerce, social media, financial, and public policy services. Thousands of data centres operate worldwide, ranging from small facilities to hyperscale complexes owned by major technology firms. The growing importance of data centres has been further intensified by recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly the development of generative AI (GenAI) models. Training and operating these models require vast computational resources, which are concentrated in and fully dependent on data centres, reinforcing their political significance. At the same time, the growth of data centres has heightened concerns about sustainability, resource consumption, environmental impact, and the uneven distribution of costs and benefits across geographies and communities. These shifts have brought attention to the technopolitics of data centres, understood as the ways in which technical design choices, governance arrangements, economic interests, and power relations shape how data centres are built, operated, and regulated. Often characterised by opacity, economic interests, geopolitical tensions, and technical complexities, data centres present challenges for public oversight and accountability. Studying data centres therefore raises methodological questions, while also offering opportunities and opening challenges for interdisciplinary research into the governance of digital infrastructure and the politics of data centres in the age of AI.

detail.abstract: UNC sYstEm L introduces a new architectural discipline through a principle‑driven mechanism designed to restore temporal coherence and structural compatibility in complex, fragmented ecosystems. Positioned above methodologies, frameworks, and operational tools, the mechanism reframes stability not as an outcome of optimization or external control, but as a function of architectural alignment and structural autoregulation. This paper establishes the theoretical foundations of temporal architecture, articulates the structural logic through which systems sustain continuity under conditions of overload and discontinuity, and defines the conditions that enable compatibility across heterogeneous entities. By presenting the mechanism exclusively at the architectural level and withholding internal procedures, the work safeguards the integrity of the discipline while offering a conceptual alternative to traditional strategic, managerial, and organizational models.

title: Power Couple? AI Growth and Renewable Energy Investment
affiliations: University of California, Irvine - Paul Merage School of Business and Johns Hopkins University - Carey Business School

detail.title: Power Couple? AI Growth and Renewable Energy Investment
detail.abstract: AI and renewable energy are increasingly framed as a “power couple”—the idea that surging AI electricity demand will accelerate clean-energy investment—yet concerns persist that AI will instead entrench fossil-fuel carbon lock-in. We reconcile these views by modeling the equilibrium interaction between AI growth and renewable investment. In a parsimonious game, a policymaker invests in renewable capacity available to AI and an AI developer chooses capability; the equilibrium depends on scaling regimes and market incentives. When the market payoff to capability is supermodular and performance gains are near-linear in compute, developers push toward frontier scale even when the marginal megawatt-hour is fossil-based. In this regime, renewable expansion can primarily relax scaling constraints rather than displace fossil generation one-for-one, weakening incentives to build enough clean capacity and reinforcing fossil dependence. This yields an “adaptation trap”: as climate damages rise, the value of AI-enabled adaptation increases, which strengthens incentives to enable frontier scaling while tolerating residual fossil use. When AI faces diminishing returns and lower scaling efficiency, energy costs discipline capability choices; renewable investment then both enables capability and decarbonizes marginal compute, generating an “adaptation pathway” in which climate stress strengthens incentives for clean-capacity expansion and can support a carbon-free equilibrium. A calibrated case study illustrates these mechanisms using observed magnitudes for investment, capability, and energy use. Decarbonizing AI is an equilibrium outcome: effective policy must keep clean capacity binding at the margin as compute expands.

detail.abstract: As sustainability initiatives are increasingly delivered through digital interfaces, understanding users’ psychological responses to technology-mediated sustainability communication is crucial in the Electronic Commerce Research and Applications. This study examines how perceived authenticity influences sustainable service usage intention through trust, and how technology anxiety functions as a boundary condition. Survey data were collected from users with experience interacting with digitally delivered sustainable services. The measurement model was validated using confirmatory factor analysis, and hypotheses were tested using regression-based mediation and moderation analyses. These findings contribute to Behaviour & Information Technology by clarifying how trust and technology anxiety jointly shape user behavior in technology-mediated sustainability contexts and by highlighting the importance of designing digital systems that support both credibility and psychological comfort.

detail.abstract:
This paper formally introduces and defines Family Cybersecurity Jurisprudence (FCJ) as an independent, interdisciplinary field of study addressing a critical and persistent gap in global cybersecurity, legal, and ethical scholarship: the systematic failure to protect the family as a coherent sociotechnical unit in cyberspace. While contemporary cybersecurity research remains predominantly technical, and existing legal, ethical, and psychological studies address digital harm in fragmented or reactive ways, no unified framework currently integrates normative authority, technical enforceability, and family-centered behavioral governance.

FCJ responds to this epistemic vacuum by establishing a jurisprudence-based cybersecurity paradigm grounded in Islamic legal theory (usūl al-fiqh and maqasid al-sharī'a), cybersecurity engineering principles, and digital family psychology. The paper conceptualizes the family not as a collection of individual users, but as an interconnected system with differentiated roles, vulnerabilities, and authority structures, particularly emphasizing the heightened risk exposure of children in digitally mediated environments.

The core contribution of this work is the formulation of the Tri-Dimensional FCJ Model, which integrates three inseparable dimensions: (1) a jurisprudential dimension that establishes normative obligations and harm hierarchies based on maqasid-oriented legal reasoning; (2) a technical dimension that translates these obligations into implementable cybersecurity controls, architectures, and risk mitigation mechanisms; and (3) an educational-behavioral dimension that cultivates digital immunity through parental governance, ethical formation, and developmental psychology. Together, these dimensions form a coherent normative-technical framework capable of addressing ideological, behavioral, technical, and economic threats targeting families in cyberspace.

Methodologically, the paper employs an interdisciplinary synthetic approach combining jurisprudential analogy (qiyās), systems thinking, and normative-technical mapping to construct a field-level theory resistant to methodological fragmentation. The framework further extends to contemporary challenges posed by artificial intelligence, articulating Sharia-guided constraints for AI deployment within family contexts and proposing governance models that balance protection, autonomy, and ethical boundaries.

Beyond theoretical formulation, FCJ advances concrete policy implications at the household, community, institutional, and state levels, and articulates a future research agenda aimed at establishing academic programs, metrics, and research institutions dedicated to family-centered cybersecurity. This paper asserts that Family Cybersecurity Jurisprudence is no longer a conceptual proposal, but a necessary and structured academic discipline required to safeguard the family under conditions of accelerating digital and algorithmic transformation.

detail.abstract:
As AI agents transition from generating text to producing side effects—writing to databases, submitting regulatory filings, executing financial transactions—the governance question shifts from connection security to decision authorization. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes how agents invoke tools, and the emerging gateway ecosystem addresses authentication, routing, and operational control. However, these layers do not produce independently verifiable evidence that a specific action complied with the governing policy in force at the time of execution.

This paper defines the “authorization boundary” for agentic AI systems in regulated environments and distinguishes access authorization (OAuth-based identity and scope verification) from action authorization (deterministic, version-bound, pre-execution evidence of policy compliance). It introduces minimum architectural requirements for evidence-grade governance—determinism under a defined governed state, temporal policy binding, and effect-token–gated execution—and proposes five anti-laundering tests for detecting superficial governance claims.

The paper argues that regulatory scrutiny is converging toward per-decision evidence rather than statistical assurance and that authorization infrastructure will become a necessary complement to MCP gateways in regulated deployments.

detail.abstract: This study examines the causal relationship between financial development and economic growth (i.e., the financegrowth nexus) in India from 1970 to 2020. It is motivated as understanding the relationship between financial development and economic growth is crucial for policy formulation, particularly in emerging economies like India. Assuming the potential nonlinearity of India's finance-growth nexus, we employ Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) and Vector Autoregression with Exogenous Variables (VARX) cointegration techniques. It is also investigated how key control variables-carbon emissions, globalization, and government expenditure-affect this nexus. Economic growth is measured by real per capita GDP, while financial development is proxied by two indicators: financial depth (the ratio of private credit to GDP) and financial efficiency (the ratio of private credit to total deposits), which is one invention of this study. Using both ARDL and VARX techniques, our findings reveal a bidirectional and non-linear relationship between financial development and economic growth, irrespective of the financial development proxy used. This bidirectional relationship highlights the intertwined nature of economic growth and financial development, suggesting that policies targeting either must consider the implications for the other, particularly within the current context of sustainable development and globalization.

title: From Poisson Brackets to Human Complexity: A Structural Genealogy of Emergence Across Science

detail.title: From Poisson Brackets to Human Complexity: A Structural Genealogy of Emergence Across Science
detail.abstract: Complex systems science is often presented as a late twentieth-century departure from reductionist physics. This paper reconstructs a continuous structural lineage beginning with the Poisson bracket as the generator of classical dynamics and tracing its transformation through statistical mechanics, thermodynamics, relativity, quantum mechanics, and quantum field theory. At each transition, core operator structure is preserved while exact reduction weakens through coarse graining, uncertainty, scale dependence, and endogenous constraints (Arnold, 1989; Dirac, 1930; Wilson, 1971). Relativity introduces a decisive shift in which spacetime geometry itself becomes dynamical (Einstein, 1915). The paper argues that contemporary socio-technical and institutional systems inherit these same constraints. Complexity is therefore not an anomaly at the edge of science but the expected consequence of interaction, information limits, and adaptive feedback across evolving state spaces.

detail.title: Trading in CEXs and DEXs with Priority Fees and Stochastic Delays
detail.abstract: We develop a mixed control framework that combines absolutely continuous controls with impulse interventions subject to stochastic execution delays. The model extends current impulse control formulations by allowing (i) the controller to choose the mean of the stochastic delay of their impulses, and allowing (ii) for multiple pending orders, so that several impulses can be submitted and executed asynchronously at random times. The framework is motivated by an optimal trading problem between centralized (CEX) and decentralized (DEX) exchanges. In DEXs, traders control the distribution of the execution delay through the priority fee paid, introducing a fundamental trade-off between delays, uncertainty, and costs. We study the optimal trading problem of a trader exploiting trading signals in CEXs and DEXs. From a mathematical perspective, we derive the associated dynamic programming principle of this new class of impulse control problems, and establish the viscosity properties of the corresponding quasi-variational inequalities. From a financial perspective, our model provides insights on how to carry out execution across CEXs and DEXs, highlighting how traders manage latency risk optimally through priority fee selection. We show that employing the optimal priority fee has a significant outperformance over non-strategic fee selection.

Innovation Sedimentation is the unmanaged accumulation of specialized personas that eventually imposes a higher cognitive load than the efficiency they provide. This paper argues that AI personas must transition from creative prompt engineering projects into "cognitive infrastructure." 
Drawing on infrastructure design logic, the author proposes a rigorous six-step lifecycle method for persona development that prioritizes functional capability over character elements. The study identifies "context entropy" as a structural maintenance condition in extended AI sessions and introduces the "Re-Grounding Maneuver" as a technical intervention. Furthermore, the paper outlines a reflexive governance framework where existing AI personas serve as adversarial reviewers to detect redundancy and "character masking" in new candidates. By establishing explicit portfolio boundaries and lifecycle management protocols, users can transform fragmented AI tools into a sustainable system of specialized thinking partners.
